newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank shares end 3.59 percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank shares end 3.59 percent lower.

text.p: Thai bank stocks tumbled 3.59 percent on Monday as economic concerns led foreign investors to reduce their exposure to Thai equities, traders said.

Bangkok Bank Plc fell four baht to 159, Krung Thai Bank Plc dropped one baht to a year low of 25.75, Thai Farmers Bank Plc fell five to 104 and Siam Commercial Bank Plc fell three to a year low of 124.
The composite SET index ended 2.19 percent down at a new six-year low of 592.18 with bank shares accounting for 26 percent of the market's volume.
"It's very hard to be exposed to Thailand without holding bank stocks in your portfolio," said one trader at a foreign broker.

Large banks have outperformed the market recently following recommendations by a number of major foreign brokers to buy major Thai bank stocks. But they are approaching new 1997 lows after a 68-point fall in the market over the last six trading sessions, traders said.
"I think the banks may be approaching attractive pricing but everybody is selling, and everything is being sold," said a senior bank analyst at a leading European broker.
Renewed currency concerns and the government's perceived failure to address a number of Thailand's economic problems were adding to selling pressure, he said.

Lower economic growth, loan quality concerns, sluggish export performance and a high interest rate environment in which the minimum lending rate is 12.75 percent, continue to undermine the market, traders said.

Though near-term sentiment remains bearish, bank stocks could post a technical rebound at week's end when details of incentives included in a planned government-backed property market rescue scheme are expected to be released, traders said.
In the longer term potential investors in bank stocks were likely to exercise caution until non-performing loan data becomes available at the end of the second quarter, the analyst said.
"But until we know what level of non-performing loans are at, or will rise to, and how far property values will fall the market will remain nervous," the analyst said.
